prior_art.edition: Busnelli 1931 opened: vol. I prints the 115 letters to Groslot in clear from the Dupuy 766 transcript; the Nota (II, just before p. 247) says ciphered places are not marked typographically in this edition. 'Pietro Giusti' is not a second writer: II p. 254 lists 'Pietro Giusto' and 'Pietro Giusti' among the pseudonyms Sarpi signed with (there, on the Castrino letters), so Mazzatinti's 'otto lettere di Pietro Giusti' are Sarpi's own letters under a cover name; Busnelli counts all 19 of ms 258 as Sarpi to Groslot.

no. 258: 'otto lettere di Pietro Giusti e di undici di Paolo Sarpi a M. de l'Isle Groslot; dal 27 maggio 1608 al 9 decembre 1610 ... Molte di quelle del Giusti sono in cifre': 8 + 11 = Busnelli's 19

1329.closed: Read in print. BnF italien 258 is the 19 Sarpi-to-Groslot letters that Busnelli, Lettere ai protestanti (Bari 1931) vol. I prints in clear as nos. IV-LV (27 May 1608 to 7 Dec 1610), from the clear transcript Dupuy 766; his Nota (vol. II pp. 249-250) names ms 258 and says it reproduces the cipher passages, and p. 254 shows 'Pietro Giusti' is a pseudonym of Sarpi, not another correspondent. Caveat: the leaves of ms 258 were not seen, so the match of each ciphered passage to the printed clear text is Busnelli's, and Mazzatinti's end date (9 Dec 1610) differs by two days from letter LV.
